solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whizz kid's very curious message, never opened

indicators.note: something never opened has had nothing done to its front, so each word here loses its first letter

parts.note: agog means eagerly curious
a letter is a written message

explanation.surface: A young prodigy receives a strange message and leaves it sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never opened' removes the first letter of both AGOG and LETTER, leaving GOG and ETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whizz kid is an ambitious, fast-rising young person, which is exactly what a go-getter is.

clue.text: Immature group of pupils in cockpit

parts.note: green means inexperienced or immature
in British schools pupils are divided into houses for sport and pastoral care

explanation.surface: A young class of schoolchildren sits in an aircraft's cockpit.
explanation.walkthrough: A school house is a British grouping of pupils across years.
explanation.definitionFit: In aviation slang a greenhouse is a glazed cockpit canopy.

clue.text: Vapid chatter to flag up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire or sag

explanation.surface: Pointless talk is used to raise a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SAG in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is empty talk or idle chatter, as in all gas.

clue.text: Occupants in temporary shelters want at heart to be housed

indicators.note: the middle letters are lodged inside the shelters

parts.note: tents are temporary shelters

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: People in makeshift shelters want, deep down, a proper home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want at heart' reads as a desire, but 'at heart' just takes the middle of want; 'to be housed' is the containment signal, apt for tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants are the people who occupy a rented property.

clue.text: Nice to see moderate article embracing acceptable opinion

indicators.note: the words hug the other piece between them

parts.note: an easy pace is a moderate one
the is the definite article
on in the sense of acceptable, as in that's not on
in my eye means in my opinion

explanation.surface: A balanced piece of writing includes a reasonable point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' acts on moderate and article together, so the acceptable piece sits between them; 'opinion' comes from the phrase in my eye, meaning in my view.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy on the eye is an idiom for attractive, pleasant to look at.

clue.text: State Senate extremely reluctant

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A legislative chamber is said to be very unwilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun (a US state with its Senate) but is the verb AVER; 'extremely' takes S and E from Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or unwilling, a direct synonym of reluctant.

clue.text: Initially en route today to block Spanish port, causing complaint

indicators.note: the letters block the port by sitting inside it

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Travellers blocked at a Spanish harbour today have cause to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' covers all three words en route today; 'to block' means sit inside. 'complaint' is the medical sense, an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a dizzy illness, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: Unfortunately, woman prematurely cancelled bill in bank

indicators.note: the other pieces go in the bank's letters

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: cancelled before the end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Greta is a woman's name
a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

explanation.surface: A woman's bill was cancelled too early, in a bank, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on; 'prematurely cancelled' means stopped before the end, so the woman loses her last letter, and 'in' places both pieces within.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrettably is a sentence adverb meaning it is a pity that, as unfortunately does.

clue.text: Jacob's missus maybe runs vessel

parts.note: Jacob is a breed of sheep, so the female of the pair is a ewe
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The biblical Jacob's wife perhaps hurries to a container.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob suggests the patriarch, but is a breed of piebald sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a kind of vessel for water.

clue.text: Simplicity of sense is a hit

indicators.note: hit in the sense of struck or knocked about, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something has the simplicity of common sense and is a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' is the anagram signal working on SENSE IS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiness is the quality of being easy, which is plain simplicity.

clue.text: Born with ancient Greek accent

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in biographies
Greek is an old slang word for a cheat or card-sharper, so the ancient sense of Greek is a rogue

explanation.surface: Someone born speaking with the accent of ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic slang 'Greek' meant a swindler; the blog notes commenters found the usage offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish lilt in speech.

clue.text: Swimming right into animal, getting hit

indicators.note: the right letter goes into the animal's word

parts.note: a beast is an animal
a stroke is a blow or hit

explanation.surface: Swimming straight into a creature, someone gets struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaststroke is a style of swimming; the noun stands in for the activity.

clue.text: Never off for Yule I suspect

parts.note: an event that is off is not on

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters that follow are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go off anywhere for Christmas, they suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges FOR YULE I into YOURLIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Not on your life is an emphatic refusal, an idiom meaning certainly not, never.

clue.text: Tissue of lies to troll about

indicators.note: about meaning around in different directions, so the letters are turned about

explanation.surface: A web of falsehoods is spread to provoke someone online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIES TO TROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet rolls are rolls of soft paper tissue.

clue.text: Regulator of company books a posh car

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A firm's regulator reads its accounts and owns a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce car.
explanation.definitionFit: A controller is a device or person that regulates something.

clue.text: Gutted officials cover up US university fails

indicators.note: the outer letters cover the other piece by sitting around it
a gutted word has its insides removed, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Disappointed officials hide the shortcomings of an American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' keeps O and S of officials; 'cover up' puts them around MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out or neglect to do it, as fails to do.

clue.text: Air foul footwear after short time

indicators.note: the shuffled footwear comes after the T

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: foul means corrupted or spoiled, so the word's letters are fouled up

explanation.surface: The smell of rank shoes hangs in the air after a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like the atmosphere the smell fouls but is a tune; 'foul' is the anagram signal and 'after' puts that anagram behind the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea for Two is a well-known song, and an air is a tune.

clue.text: Hard work securing support for backing mass confection

indicators.note: one piece holds the others fast inside it

parts.note: sweat is toil or hard labour

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for support is read in reverse

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Laborious work keeps up the backing for some large sugary treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for backing' reverses only the support, and 'mass' follows it; 'securing' then holds both inside the hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is an old word for a sweet or candied delicacy, a confection.

clue.text: Swing music introduced by kid on the radio

indicators.note: the music is introduced into the kid's word
on the radio means as heard spoken, so the word's sound is used

parts.note: to kid is to tease
rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: Swing music is presented by a youngster on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' applies to kid only: tease said aloud is spelt to fit the answer's ending; 'introduced by' slots the music after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a swinging bar used by acrobats, a kind of swing.

clue.text: Custom somewhat hard at first

indicators.note: the hard letter is placed first, before the other piece

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a bit means to some extent, somewhat

explanation.surface: A tradition that was a little difficult to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a settled practice, the same as a custom.

clue.text: Notice call to effort

definitions.meaning: to give someone the ... is to dismiss them, like giving notice
the sailors' cry when hauling together

explanation.surface: Notice a call to make an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave-ho is both a dismissal and a rhythmic chant urging workers to pull.

clue.text: Willing girlfriend coming to game — it's a start

parts.note: ready means willing or prepared
a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: An eager girlfriend joins in a game, and that is how it begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, steady, go is the call that begins a race, so it is a start.

clue.text: Bed made of mostly turned wood

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters are read in reverse
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: birch is a wood

explanation.surface: A bed is built from mostly recycled timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BIRCH to BIRC; 'turned' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a baby's bed with high barred sides, a cot.

clue.text: Aid learner, one cutting the knot?

indicators.note: the pieces cut into the knot, splitting it apart

parts.note: a reef knot is the common square knot
L is for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A student helps someone slice through the tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts L and I inside REEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is help given to people in need, such as famine aid.

clue.text: Impressive flower up for arrangement

indicators.note: a flower arrangement suggests the letters being arranged anew

explanation.surface: A striking bloom is put forward for a floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges FLOWER UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something powerful has a strong effect, so it is impressive.

clue.text: Thick offender having stumbled in seconds

indicators.note: in seconds means taking the second letter of each word

explanation.surface: A stupid criminal who tripped is caught in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in seconds' looks like 'very quickly' but takes F, A, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick and fat both describe something wide or bulky.

clue.text: Hamper opinion surrounding request

indicators.note: one word sits around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: my bet is means my opinion is
to ask is to make a request

explanation.surface: An opinion hampers a request someone made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a wicker basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded wicker basket, often for picnic food.

clue.text: Hack back old-fashioned, short frizzy hairdo

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: retro means imitating an old style

indicators.note: short means missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a perm is a chemically curled hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back an outdated, cropped curly style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims PERM to PER; 'back' reverses RETROPER as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack is a disparaging word for a journalist, a reporter.
